reason: Robert clarified that avatar likeness refs, clothing/outfit refs, and bedroom/world refs were getting mixed together.
core_answer: Clothing/outfits are both Avatar Builder and World Builder work, but they own different parts.
avatar_builder_owns: nude/base body maturity policy and body topology
wearable garment meshes fitted to one avatar body
garment rigging, cloth simulation, collision, thickness, openings, grab points, and fasteners
avatar wardrobe slots and per-character outfit compatibility
lip sync, eye movement, facial expressions, and head/neck controls
world_builder_owns: places where clothes, towels, blankets, and bedding exist in the world
stores that sell clothing, towels, blankets, bedding, and accessories
closets, shelves, drawers, racks, laundry baskets, dressing rooms, and store displays
blankets on beds, towels in bathrooms, folded clothes on shelves, and loose cloth props
world inventory records that reference wardrobe items without rebuilding avatar meshes
Paris notebook world rooms such as Marinette's home and bedroom
shared_contract: World Builder can place a shirt as a hanging/store/folded world object.
Avatar Builder must provide the wearable version and dressing state machine.
The same item can have two linked forms: a world prop form and a wearable avatar garment form.
When an AI buys, grabs, or chooses clothing in the world, the world item hands off to Avatar Builder for fitting and dressing.
After dressing finishes, the worn garment must be a stable rigged/cloth garment, not a floating stored prop.
When the AI removes the garment, Avatar Builder returns it to a world prop state so World Builder can place it folded in a drawer, hanging in a closet, in a laundry basket, or on a store rack.

reference_routing.avatar_head_body: clean character or person photos from correct source and maturity policy only
reference_routing.wardrobe_builder: outfit photos, costume designs, fabric closeups, seams, collars, sleeves, shoes, bags, jewelry
reference_routing.reject_for_likeness: voice actors, live-action actors, cosplayers, fan art, toys, dolls, product shots, unrelated people

maturity_rule: Non-adult avatars remain doll-safe below the neck.
Adult avatars may use adult anatomy references only for anatomy-guided base body construction.
Outfits for non-adult avatars must not require adult anatomy references.
